lessonRef.subject: ready-for-life
lessonRef.title: Application or project: utilities, safety devices, and shutoffs

objective: Learners locate and record the location of four real household safety points, the main water shutoff, the main electrical panel, the nearest fire extinguisher, and every smoke or carbon-monoxide detector, then test one detector's function under adult supervision, so they can act quickly in a real emergency.
scenario: With a trusted adult guiding a walk-through of the real home, the learner locates and writes down or sketches the location of four safety points, confirms with the adult that each is currently accessible and unobstructed, and tests one smoke or carbon-monoxide detector using its built-in test button.
safetyNotes: The learner does not operate the main water shutoff or electrical panel during this lesson; locating and identifying them is enough.
Detector testing uses only the device's built-in test button, done with the adult present.
Completing this task sheet never certifies the walk-through by itself; a guardian confirmation is required before the task counts as complete, exactly as this course's own safety policy states.

simulationAlternative.description: If a real walk-through is not possible, the learner instead studies a floor plan (their own drawn sketch or a provided sample) and marks where each of the four safety points would typically be located in a home of that layout, explaining the reasoning for each placement.

materials: access to the real home with a trusted adult
paper or a notes app to record locations
a working smoke or carbon-monoxide detector with a test button

tasks.directions: Before the walk-through, predict where you think each of the four safety points is located.

prompts.text: Write your best guess for the location of each of the four safety points before checking with your adult.

tasks.directions: With your adult, walk through the home and confirm the real location of each safety point, noting whether it is currently accessible and unobstructed.

prompts.text: I recorded the confirmed location of the main water shutoff and whether it is accessible.
I recorded the confirmed location of the main electrical panel and whether it is accessible.
I recorded the confirmed location of the nearest fire extinguisher and its expiration status if visible.
I recorded the location of every smoke or carbon-monoxide detector I could find.

tasks.directions: With your adult present, press the test button on one detector and note the result.

prompts.text: Did the tested detector sound correctly when the test button was pressed?
If it did not respond, what did your adult say the next step should be?

tasks.directions: Compare your predictions from the warm-up to what you actually found.

prompts.text: Which safety point's real location most surprised you compared to your prediction, and why does knowing its exact location matter in an actual emergency?

remediation: If a learner cannot distinguish the main electrical panel from a subpanel or an unrelated box, reteach with labeled photos of the two side by side, naming the specific visual features (a single large panel with a main breaker at the top versus a smaller box with fewer switches) before returning to the real walk-through.
extension: Have the learner draw a simple floor plan marking all four safety points and add a fifth point of their own choosing, such as a first-aid kit location, explaining why they added it.
